seal.statement: An authoritative service-lifecycle reconciliation of the system-table cache never installs a services row that claims a version newer than the columns it carries: when the authoritative row read from the services partition is newer than the cached row, the cached row afterwards holds the authoritative value of every column the authoritative row carries, including raft_role; an absent (null or missing) cached value never overrides an authoritative value; and the refresh reports the cache aligned only when the cached row agrees with the authoritative row on every authoritative column, or the cached row is strictly newer.

text: Transition record and scope before any edit (base 9a22bf79b, rule-set revision 5). Cause traced read-only on ed708dfd and reproduced deterministically; analysis retained at lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/partial-row-cache-write-analysis.md. 1 Producer/consumer: trigger confirmActiveReplicaTerminalHandoff (src/rebalancer operation-workflow-recovery-status-reconcile) -> refreshAuthoritativeReplicaCacheRow -> refreshAuthoritativeCacheRow (cdc-integration-service-cache-visibility-wait: SELECT * full row, lifecycle mode forced for services) -> applyAuthoritativeCacheRepairRow -> applySystemTableChange (mutation mode authoritative_service_lifecycle_reconciliation, which skips isStaleForExistingRecord and always reports incomingVersionAccepted) -> buildAuthoritativeServiceLifecycleCacheReplacement (src/cache/system-table-cache-authoritative-reconciliation.js): starts from the cached row, copies authoritative fields only where the cached row lacks the key, overlays lifecycle fields when the authoritative durable version is >= the cached one, labels updated_at = max, then applyPreservedNonLeaderVoterRaftRole. Consumers: about 25 readers of raft_role (remove-safety, budget, move/surplus planning, learner promotion, readiness surplus, CAS guards, priority-spread projection) and areAuthoritativeSystemTableCacheRowsAligned, whose true answer lets the handoff complete. 2 Shape: the services row as read from the services partition; no new type. 3 Identity/generation: row key (service id); durable version column resolved by resolveServiceDurableVersion; updated_at is the cache's version label; updated_at_hlc exists only on CDC-delivered rows and is legitimately dropped when superseded. 4 Ordering: authority newer than cache => authority's columns; cache strictly newer => cache row kept (existing contract); equal version => every authoritative column must agree for aligned, and absent cached content never wins. 5 Absent vs unavailable: a null/missing cached column is absent evidence, never newer evidence; an unreadable authority stays the existing typed refusal. 6 Durable commit: none changes; the cache is a projection. 7 Retained obligations: none; a later CDC event for the same row still applies under the ordinary version fence. 8 Wake/cleanup: unchanged. Writable paths: src/cache/system-table-cache-authoritative-reconciliation.js, src/cache/system-table-cache.js only where this mode's apply consumes the builder, test/cache/system-table-cache-services-lifecycle-merge.test.js, test/rebalancer/operation-workflow-active-cache-handoff.test.js and one new real-consumer witness. Excluded: every consumer of raft_role, CDC delivery, HLC stamping, bounds, journey predicates. History to respect: CL-021 (701db25fa), CL-035/CL-016, quest executor-active-services-cache-handoff ('preserve newer evidence'); merge body present since 3bf3f2406; the wip/formation-integration line has a byte-identical builder and no repair. Wider question recorded for the epic, not absorbed here: whether any cache row may be ahead of durable authority at all (owner rule 2026-11-02: the cache never grants).
